headline: A preprint measures correlated errors across LLM judges and shows when consensus overstates evidence
summary: The authors of arXiv:2609.22512 report correlated errors across open-weight and frontier LLM judges. In their main ten-judge open-weight bank, average pairwise error correlation is 0.206 and the variance-based effective ensemble size is 3.51 on 1,133 RewardBench preference pairs; this is not a claim about majority-vote accuracy. In resampled 100-pair Focus panels, a pooled-vote significance test disagrees with an item-level test in 28% of panels. Three cross-provider frontier judges show error correlation of 0.56 on RewardBench, based on a small bank and relatively few residual errors. The authors find that different error structures favor different filters, while their tested dependence-aware filters do not outperform plain majority on the screened factuality and code settings. These are preprint results, not independently reproduced findings.
